content.text: USER: make me an online multiplayer game i can play with my friends. I want it to be like super smash bros. a 2D platform fighter. generate all the assets, make realistic fighting animations for each character and everything. on the start screen we wait for everyone to join, then the next screen is character selection, then the next screen is map selection, then we start the battle. each character has 3 lives. if they fall off they lose a life, last player standing wins and the cycle repeats.

content.thinking:
The user wants a full-fledged online multiplayer 2D platform fighter reminiscent of Super Smash Bros, with all assets, realistic fighting animations, lobby flow, character selection, map selection, lives system, etc. This is an extremely large scope: it involves server-side networking, authoritative physics, client rendering, asset generation, animation pipelines, sound, UI flow, and more. I need to respond appropriately: I can't instantly deliver a complete game, but I can outline a plan and start building it. First, I should acknowledge the request and summarize what I will create, showing that I understand the components: a Node.js WebSocket server for matchmaking, physics, and game state; a HTML5 canvas client handling rendering, input, and animations; procedural generation of characters and assets to meet the "generate all the assets" demand; skeletal animation system for realistic fighting moves; map and particle effects; sound integration; and the lobby flow (waiting room, character selection, map selection, battle). I also need to be transparent about checking the execution environment (e.g., whether the sandbox supports Node.js, WebSocket, canvas, etc.) before proceeding. This will set expectations and allow me to adapt the implementation to the available tools. Therefore, the most suitable next message is a concise description of the intended architecture and a statement that I will first verify the environment. This aligns with the user's request and prepares for the next steps.
I'll build you a complete 2D platform fighter — Node.js WebSocket server (authoritative physics, lobbies, stocks) plus a canvas client with procedurally generated characters, skeletal fighting animations, maps, particles, and sound. Let me check the environment first.
